rice.fertilizer: Apply Nitrogen-rich fertilizers in split doses (e.g., Urea). Ensure adequate Phosphorus (DAP) at planting and Potassium for grain filling.
rice.watering: Maintain standing water (5-10 cm) during early vegetative stages. Drain water 10-15 days before harvesting.
rice.soil_care: Clayey or clay loam soils that retain moisture are ideal. Prepare soil by puddling (tilling in water) to reduce percolation loss.
rice.harvesting: Harvest when 80-85% of the grains turn straw-colored and moisture content drops to around 20%.

maize.fertilizer: Requires balanced N-P-K. Apply Nitrogen at knee-high and tasseling stages, and Phosphorus during land preparation.
maize.watering: Irrigate at critical stages: tasseling, silking, and grain filling. Avoid waterlogging which damages roots.
maize.soil_care: Well-drained sandy loam to clay loam soils. Ensure deep tillage to allow roots to penetrate deep.
maize.harvesting: Harvest when the moisture content is 20-25% and the husks turn yellow-brown.

chickpea.fertilizer: Requires low Nitrogen as it is a legume. Apply Starter Nitrogen and balanced Phosphorus/Sulfur.
chickpea.watering: Highly drought-tolerant. Irrigate once at branching and once at pod-development stage if rain is scarce.
chickpea.soil_care: Sandy clay loam or well-drained loamy soils. Avoid saline or alkaline soils, and maintain loose soil bed.
chickpea.harvesting: Harvest when leaves turn yellow and pods dry out. Grains should rattle inside the pods.

kidneybeans.fertilizer: Legume crop, but benefits from starter Nitrogen and moderate Phosphorus. Avoid excessive Nitrogen as it delays maturity.
kidneybeans.watering: Keep soil uniformly moist but not soggy. Irrigate during flowering and pod development.
kidneybeans.soil_care: Light loam to clay loam soils with good drainage. Extremely sensitive to waterlogging.
kidneybeans.harvesting: Harvest when pods turn dry, straw-colored, and brittle.

pigeonpies.fertilizer: Apply a starter dose of Nitrogen along with Phosphorus. Rhizobium inoculation helps nitrogen fixation.
pigeonpies.watering: Grows well under rainfed conditions. Provide irrigation during flower initiation and pod filling if dry.
pigeonpies.soil_care: Requires deep, well-drained loamy or clayey soils. Sensitive to waterlogging.
pigeonpies.harvesting: Harvest when 75-80% of the pods turn brown and dry.

mothbeans.fertilizer: Drought-hardy legume. Minimal fertilizer needed. Apply starter Phosphorus.
mothbeans.watering: Extremely drought-resistant. Only water during severe, prolonged dry spells.
mothbeans.soil_care: Sandy or light-textured soils with excellent drainage. Can tolerate poor soils.
mothbeans.harvesting: Harvest when pods turn yellowish-brown and are fully dry.

mungbean.fertilizer: Rhizobium treatment recommended. Apply starter N and moderate P.
mungbean.watering: Requires 2-3 irrigations: at branching, flowering, and pod-filling stages. Highly sensitive to waterlogging.
mungbean.soil_care: Well-drained loamy to sandy loam soils. Maintain neutral pH.
mungbean.harvesting: Harvest in multiple pickings as pods mature, or cut whole plant when 80% of pods turn black.

blackgram.fertilizer: Apply starter Nitrogen and Phosphorus. Use Biofertilizers like Phosphobacteria for better yield.
blackgram.watering: Water at flowering and pod filling. Keep soil moist but avoid waterlogging.
blackgram.soil_care: Loamy to clayey soils with good drainage. Can tolerate slightly heavier soils than mungbeans.
blackgram.harvesting: Harvest when pods turn dark brown or black and dry out.

lentil.fertilizer: Requires starter Nitrogen and high Phosphorus. Sulfur application improves grain quality.
lentil.watering: Grows well on residual moisture. Water once or twice at flowering and pod filling if soil is dry.
lentil.soil_care: Well-drained light loams to clay loams. Tolerates acidic soils better than other pulses.
lentil.harvesting: Harvest when the plants turn yellow and pods dry up, but before they split open.

pomegranate.fertilizer: Apply organic manure annually. Supplement with balanced N-P-K, Zinc, and Boron during flowering and fruit set.
pomegranate.watering: Drip irrigation is highly recommended. Regular watering during fruit growth prevents fruit cracking.
pomegranate.soil_care: Well-drained sandy loam or alluvial soils. Tolerates mild alkalinity and salinity.
pomegranate.harvesting: Harvest when fruits turn yellowish-red and give a metallic sound when tapped.

banana.fertilizer: Heavy feeder. Requires high Potassium and Nitrogen. Apply in regular monthly split doses.
banana.watering: Requires high moisture. Maintain uniform moisture around root zone. Drip irrigation is highly recommended.
banana.soil_care: Rich, deep, well-drained loamy soil with high organic matter. Keep pH between 6.0 and 7.5.
banana.harvesting: Harvest bunches when the fruits turn plump, green angles start flattening, and top leaves begin drying.

mango.fertilizer: Apply Nitrogen and Potassium to young trees. Mature trees require Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potassium, and micronutrients after harvest.
mango.watering: Irrigate young plants regularly. Mature trees need irrigation during fruit development but dry period before flowering.
mango.soil_care: Deep, well-drained loamy or alluvial soils. Avoid soils with hard pan layers.
mango.harvesting: Harvest when fruits start changing color from green to light yellow, and a few ripe fruits fall naturally.

grapes.fertilizer: Apply Nitrogen during early growth, and Potassium during berry development. Zinc and Boron prevent fruit drop.
grapes.watering: Drip irrigation is preferred. Reduce watering during ripening stage to increase sugar content.
grapes.soil_care: Sandy loam to gravelly loam soils with good drainage. Grapes prefer slightly acidic to neutral pH.
grapes.harvesting: Harvest when grapes reach full color, sweetness, and the stems turn brown.

watermelon.fertilizer: Apply Phosphorus-heavy fertilizer at planting. Switch to Nitrogen/Potassium when vines start running.
watermelon.watering: Requires abundant watering during growth and flowering. Reduce watering as fruits ripen to prevent bursting.
watermelon.soil_care: Sandy loam soils that warm up quickly are best. Ensure high organic content.
watermelon.harvesting: Harvest when the underside spot turns creamy-yellow, and the tendril near the fruit dries up.

muskmelon.fertilizer: Requires balanced N-P-K. Apply Nitrogen during vine growth and Potassium during fruit enlargement.
muskmelon.watering: Irrigate regularly. Avoid overhead watering to prevent leaf diseases. Reduce watering before harvest.
muskmelon.soil_care: Sandy loam or loamy soils with high drainage. Prefers warm soil temperatures.
muskmelon.harvesting: Harvest at 'full slip' stage (when the stem separates easily from the fruit with light pressure).

apple.fertilizer: Apply balanced N-P-K and Calcium annually. Calcium prevents bitter pit disorder in apples.
apple.watering: Requires regular moisture, especially during bloom and fruit set. Avoid waterlogging around root collar.
apple.soil_care: Deep, well-drained loamy soils. Maintain organic mulch around trees to conserve moisture.
apple.harvesting: Harvest when the skin color develops fully, flesh is firm, and starch-iodine test indicates ripeness.

orange.fertilizer: Requires regular Nitrogen, Zinc, Iron, and Manganese. Apply fertilizers 3-4 times a year.
orange.watering: Irrigate regularly, avoiding dry spells followed by heavy watering (causes fruit splitting).
orange.soil_care: Deep, well-drained sandy loam or clay loam soils. Avoid soils with high water tables.
orange.harvesting: Harvest when fruits turn fully orange and develop sweet taste. Cut with clippers.

papaya.fertilizer: Fast grower. Requires heavy and frequent application of Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Potassium.
papaya.watering: Keep soil moist but not wet. Extremely sensitive to waterlogging (causes root rot in 48 hours).
papaya.soil_care: Sandy loam soils with excellent drainage and high organic matter. Maintain pH of 6.0 - 6.5.
papaya.harvesting: Harvest when latex turns clear rather than milky, and skin shows yellow streaks (color break).

coconut.fertilizer: Apply high Potassium (Muriate of Potash), Nitrogen, and Magnesium. Supplement with common salt (sodium).
coconut.watering: Requires plenty of water. Irrigate during dry months (drip or basin irrigation).
coconut.soil_care: Sandy loam, alluvial, or lateritic soils. Can tolerate sandy coastal soils if water table is accessible.
coconut.harvesting: Harvest fully mature nuts (11-12 months old) for copra/oil, or tender nuts (7-8 months old) for water.

cotton.fertilizer: Requires high Nitrogen (apply in splits) and balanced Phosphorus/Potassium. Boron is essential for boll development.
cotton.watering: Irrigate at critical stages: squaring, flowering, and boll development. Reduce watering during boll opening.
cotton.soil_care: Deep black soils (regur) or deep loams with good water retention and drainage.
cotton.harvesting: Harvest (pick) when bolls are fully open and dry. Avoid picking wet cotton.

jute.fertilizer: Apply Nitrogen in split doses. Supplement with moderate Phosphorus and Potassium during land preparation.
jute.watering: Requires high rainfall and humidity. Flood irrigation or heavy moisture is necessary during early growth.
jute.soil_care: Alluvial sandy loam or clay loam soils found in river basins. Tolerates waterlogging after early growth.
jute.harvesting: Harvest at the small pod/flowering stage (120-135 days) to get the best quality fiber.

coffee.fertilizer: Apply balanced N-P-K. Requires higher Nitrogen and Potassium. Micronutrients like Zinc and Boron are vital.
coffee.watering: Requires well-distributed rainfall. A dry period of 2-3 months is needed before blossom showers.
coffee.soil_care: Deep, rich, organic, acidic soils (pH 5.0 - 6.0) under shade tree canopy. Excellent drainage is critical.
coffee.harvesting: Harvest only the fully ripe, bright red cherries (selective picking) for premium quality.
